summary: Declare the flights command's optional positionals as separate brackets ([origin] [destination] [date]) so the MCP mirror exposes each as its own tool property and passes them as separate argv elements.
reason: The MCP cobratree mirror maps each bracket token in a command's Use string to one schema property and one argv element; a combined [origin destination date] group made the flights tool unusable positionally over MCP ("accepts 3 arg(s), received 1"), which also blocked the --select-outbound return-leg flow since it cannot combine with --trip.
validated_outcome: go test ./internal/mcp -run TestMCPFlightsToolExposesSeparatePositionals fails on the old Use string and passes on the new one; an MCP tools/call with {origin, destination, date} reaches gflights.Search(AMS -> BCN on 2026-10-16).
